newsitem.title: UK: Man sees cocoa deficit 170-230,000 T in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Man sees cocoa deficit 170-230,000 T in 1996/97.

text.p: World cocoa production deficit in the 1996/97 season (Oct/Sept) should be between 170,000 and 230,000 tonnes due to strong consumption and an estimated decline in output, traders E.D.&F. Man said on Thursday.
It said the exceptionally favourable weather conditions in West Africa last season which helped to push stocks to nearly 1.2 million tonnes appeared to be absent this year.
In its January report, Man forecast output in top grower Ivory Coast around 1.050 million tonnes against an estimated 1.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.
"West African arrivals have been lower this year than last season," it said.

World cocoa production was expected to fall by 10 percent from 1995/96 to 2.586 million tonnes. The growth in Indonesian production was slowing with the total harvest now put at 310,000 tonnes. This compared with the 1995/96 estimate of 290,000 tonnes.
Brazil was facing its poorest crop since 1968/69 due to weather problems. "We expect production in 1996/97 to total 156,000 tonnes," Man said.
The estimate for Brazil in 1995/96 was 219,000 tonnes.
Man forecast an increase in world grindings of 2.5-3.0 percent in 1996/97 to 2.762 million tonnes.
"Much of this extra grind will occur at origin with significant increases expected in West africa and the Far East," Man said.
